local_adaptation: Requested visual adaptation, distinct from static official observations: both views submit the first flight immediately when using equipment, before native moveDelete. Self origin is the actual hand card; other origin is the actual portrait center. Neither view waits for notification or between flight phases. Later notifications never restart a flight. Self:300ms full-size flight to the lower window center(cx,cy-175), then the source-confirmed433.333ms EaseSineIn move to the actual portrait, then the source-confirmed subtype slot duration and scale targets. Other:following the user request to further extend the40% outward route, fly60% toward the stack center over200ms (slightly slowed from160ms); the slot start reads the completed entry animation duration to avoid stale handoff offsets while retaining full card size, then immediately enter the actual equip slot. This distance/duration is a requested local adapter, not an official constant. For smooth handoffs, remove the official 200ms post-portrait hold/fade, keep opacity 1 across both joins, and preserve scale at every boundary. Opacity decreases continuously during the slot flight, from 1 to 0.9 before the final 100ms, then to 0 at the slot center. This retains the requested fade during motion and gives the strongest fade the same 100ms window as the official client. All phases use Web Animations. The first animation is submitted paused at currentTime0 and begins only once the card face is visible. Self animations keep native playback. Other-seat animations stay paused and advance currentTime on rendered requestAnimationFrame callbacks, capping each increment at40ms. This preserves both visible legs when a long settlement task blocks drawing; the prior wall-clock chaining could expire both legs under a520ms stall. Each segment endpoint remains for one render before completing. Only host/layout changes recalculate geometry; the visual clock does not read layout or write DOM styles. A3s initial readiness timeout restores equipment and releases any waiter. Actual equipment follows native rule settlement immediately and remains hidden until the visual flight finishes. Per the latest user request, non-self locally executed useCard only (excluding game.online receiving clients/replay) inserts an after event awaiting that flight completion Promise. This holds the next parent action until the equipment appears; self useCard does not wait. Completion, cancellation, removal, style change and readiness timeout all resolve the same flight Promise. No global pause/resume, native waitingForTransition token, early equip call or synthetic equipment card is introduced. No horse skip or consecutive-use heuristic.
